repeated measurements of the same individuals over decades (to separate shrinkage from cohort/secular effects)

datasets.name: CDC National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey — Body Measures (BMX) and Demographics (DEMO) files

checked.method: HEAD access_url and DEMO_J.xpt; GET BMX_J.htm codebook; HEAD 1999 BMX.xpt

variables_present: measured standing height per adult individual (BMXHT, cm)
age at measurement (RIDAGEYR in DEMO file, top-coded at 80)
variables_missing: repeated measurements of the same individuals
datasets.scope: US civilian non-institutionalized population, cross-sectional, 2-year cycles 1999–2018 and later; each cycle ~9,000 examined persons of all ages
datasets.evidence: BMX_J.xpt HEAD 200, Content-Length 1466000; DEMO_J.xpt HEAD 200, Content-Length 3412720; codebook BMX_J.htm lists 'BMXHT - Standing Height (cm)'; 1999-2000 BMX.xpt HEAD 200, 2827840 bytes. Both assessor URLs (www.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/ and wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/) returned 200. Note: the older file path wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Nhanes/2017-2018/BMX_J.XPT returns a 200 HTML 'Page Not Found' page; the Public/<year>/DataFiles path works. Age is top-coded at 80 in public DEMO files, limiting 'extreme old age'.

search_log.note: Mostly forestry; one relevant item is a paper/figshare record 10.25405/ncl.34621644 'Self-report overestimates true height loss' (Newcastle), a publication not a measured-height dataset
Top hits are birth-cohort survey-mapping documents; no stature-by-age dataset in the first page

search_log.query: title:(stature OR height) AND title:age AND title:adult, type=dataset

summary: NHANES Body Measures files (BMXHT standing height, with RIDAGEYR age in DEMO) are openly downloadable as SAS transport files for every 2-year cycle since 1999 and give measured adult stature by age, but cross-sectionally and with age top-coded at 80, so they mix shrinkage with secular trend and cannot reach 'extreme old age'. HRS, the one longitudinal source named, returned 403 to curl and needs registration. No repository dataset of repeated measured heights in the same adults was found in DataCite, Zenodo or Dryad.
next_step: Pre-register a cross-sectional NHANES test (pooled 1999–2018 BMXHT by RIDAGEYR, 20–80, sex-stratified) as a first pass; for the timing claim register for HRS or a European panel (ELSA/SHARE) to get within-person height change across waves.
obstacles_confirmed: Cross-sectional height-by-age mixes shrinkage with the secular increase in peak height.
Longitudinal series that separate those effects are less directly downloadable than NHANES (HRS site blocks anonymous access).
NHANES public age is top-coded at 80, so 'extreme old age' is not resolvable there.
